ei.title: The Universality of Basic Human Emotions
ei.subject: 수능특강

fullPassage: The issue of cultural variation in emotions has been controversial. At first, it was widely believed that different cultures produced radically different emotional states, so that a person from one culture could not even begin to understand what someone from another culture was feeling. This view received a severe blow from evidence that people from very different cultures could translate emotion words effectively and even recognize facial expressions of emotion. A highly influential research program by Paul Ekman and his associates began with photographs of facial expressions that Americans would easily recognize as expressing different basic emotions: angry, sad, happy, and the like. Ekman and his group traveled all over the world showing the photographs to people in widely different cultures, including even some distant tribes that had had almost no contact with Western civilization. By and large, most people in every culture recognized the emotions expressed in those American faces. These results convinced most doubters that some aspects of emotions are innate and universal.

questions.passage: The issue of cultural variation in emotions has been ①<u>controversial</u>. At first, it was widely ②<u>believing</u> that different cultures ③<u>produced</u> radically different emotional states, so that a person from one culture could not even begin to understand what someone from another culture was feeling. This view received a severe blow from evidence that people from very different cultures could translate emotion words ④<u>effectively</u> and even recognize facial expressions of emotion. A highly influential research program by Paul Ekman and his associates began with photographs of facial expressions that Americans would easily recognize as expressing different basic emotions: angry, sad, happy, and the like. Ekman and his group traveled all over the world showing the photographs to people in widely different cultures, including even some distant tribes that had had almost no contact with Western civilization. By and large, most people in every culture recognized the emotions expressed in those American faces. These results convinced most doubters that some aspects of emotions are innate and universal.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① controversial=논란이 많은(형용사 보어 정상), ② believed→believing 오류(수동태 was believed가 맞음), ③ produced=만들어냈다(동사 과거형 정상), ④ effectively=효과적으로(부사 정상)
det.analysis:
❌ ① controversial: 'has been controversial' — 주격보어 형용사 정상
✅ ② believing: 'it was widely believing that' — 수동태 was believed가 맞음. believing(현재분사)은 수동태 불가
❌ ③ produced: 'different cultures produced' — 과거형 동사 정상
❌ ④ effectively: 'translate emotion words effectively' — 동사 수식 부사 정상
det.tip: It was believed that~ = ~라고 믿어졌다 (수동태). believing은 수동태에 쓸 수 없음

det.korean: ① influential=영향력 있는(형용사 정상), ② expressing=표현하는(현재분사 정상), ③ traveled=여행했다(과거형 정상), ④ recognized→recognizing 오류(주절 동사 자리에 현재분사 불가)

✅ ④ recognizing: 'most people in every culture recognizing the emotions' — 주절의 주어 most people에 대한 서술어가 필요. recognizing(현재분사)은 주절 동사 역할 불가. recognized가 맞음

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① what=~하는 것(관계대명사 정상), ② began=시작했다(과거형 정상), ③ had had→have had 오류(대과거 had had가 맞음), ④ convinced=확신시켰다(과거형 정상)
det.analysis:
❌ ① what: 'understand what someone from another culture was feeling' — 관계대명사 what 정상
❌ ② began: 'A highly influential research program began' — 과거형 동사 정상
✅ ③ have had: 'tribes that have had almost no contact' — 주절 traveled(과거)보다 이전 시점이므로 대과거 had had가 맞음. have had(현재완료)는 시제 불일치
❌ ④ convinced: 'These results convinced most doubters' — 과거형 동사 정상

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ①what=무엇(←that 접속사가 맞음, 명사절 내 SVO 완전), ②easily=쉽게(부사 정상), ③showing=보여주며(분사구문 정상), ④expressed=표현된(과거분사 정상)
det.analysis:
✅ ① what: 'it was widely believed what different cultures produced...' — believe의 목적어인 명사절에서 produced의 목적어(emotional states)가 이미 있으므로 관계대명사 what 불가. 접속사 that이 맞음
❌ ② easily: 'Americans would easily recognize' — 동사 수식 부사 정상
❌ ③ showing: 'traveled all over the world showing' — 분사구문(~하면서) 정상
❌ ④ expressed: 'the emotions expressed in those American faces' — 과거분사 수식 정상
det.tip: that절: 완전한 문장 → 접속사 that. what절: 불완전한 문장(목적어/주어 빈자리) → 관계대명사 what. 여기는 완전한 문장이므로 that

A highly influential research program by Paul Ekman and his associates began with photographs of facial expressions that Americans would easily recognize as expressing different basic emotions: angry, sad, happy, and the like. By and large, most people in every culture recognized the emotions expressed in those American faces. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ①narrowly(좁게←widely) ②radically(근본적으로) ③severe(심각한) ④universal(보편적인)
det.analysis:
✅ ① narrowly: 원문은 widely(넓게). '좁게 믿어졌다'는 '넓게 믿어졌다'라는 원문과 반대 ←정답
❌ ② radically: '근본적으로' 다른 감정 상태라는 맥락에 적절
❌ ③ severe: 기존 견해에 '심한' 타격이라는 맥락에 적절
❌ ④ universal: 감정의 일부가 '보편적'이라는 결론에 적절
det.tip: widely(넓게) ↔ narrowly(좁게). widely believed = 널리 믿어졌다

questions.passage: The issue of cultural ①<u>variation</u> in emotions has been controversial. A highly influential research program by Paul Ekman and his associates began with photographs of facial expressions that Americans would easily recognize as expressing different basic emotions: angry, sad, happy, and the like. Ekman and his group traveled all over the world showing the photographs to people in widely different cultures, including even some ②<u>neighboring</u> tribes that had had almost no contact with Western civilization. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 먼(distant) 부족들까지 포함했다. neighboring(이웃한)은 distant의 반의어로 부적절.
det.analysis:
❌ ① variation — 원문 일치. '문화적 차이'라는 맥락에 적절
✅ ② neighboring — 원문은 distant(먼). 서구 문명과 접촉이 거의 없는 '먼' 부족이어야 연구의 의미가 있음. neighboring(이웃한)으로 바꾸면 서구 영향이 있을 수 있어 보편성 증거 약화
❌ ③ recognized — 원문 일치. 모든 문화에서 감정을 '인식했다'는 맥락에 적절
❌ ④ innate — 원문 일치. 감정의 일부가 '타고난' 것이라는 결론에 적절
det.tip: distant tribes that had had almost no contact with Western civilization. 먼 부족 = 서구 접촉 없음 = 보편성 증거의 핵심

det.korean: 첫 문장 'has been controversial'과 일치하는가?
det.analysis:
✅ T: 'The issue of cultural variation in emotions has been controversial' — '논란이 많았다'는 의견이 엇갈려 왔다는 의미와 일치
❌ F: 본문과 불일치

questions.stem: 에크만의 연구 결과, 감정 표현의 인식은 모든 문화에서 완전히 동일한 것으로 나타났다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 기존 견해가 증거로부터 '심한 타격'을 받았다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① radically different emotional states: 초기 견해 내용이지 receive의 목적어로 부적절
❌ ② facial expressions of emotion: 연구 자료이지 견해가 받는 것이 아님
✅ ③ a severe blow from evidence: 'This view received ____' — 기존 견해가 증거로부터 심한 타격
❌ ④ different basic emotions: 사진의 내용이지 견해가 받는 것이 아님
det.tip: This view received a severe blow = 이 견해는 심한 타격을 받았다. from evidence = 증거로부터

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 사람들이 감정 단어를 번역하고 감정의 '얼굴 표정'까지 인식할 수 있었다.
det.analysis:

questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: ④ 에크만이 전 세계에서 사진을 보여줌 — 본문 일치
